original_query: SELECT t12.SAL FROM (SELECT * FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, SLACKER, SAL AS SAL0, SAL = 4 AS f9 FROM EMPNULLABLES WHERE DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000) AS t11 WHERE SAL > 1000) AS t12 INNER JOIN (SELECT t14.SAL, t17.SAL AS SAL0, t17.f9 FROM (SELECT EMPNO, ENAME, JOB, MGR, HIREDATE, SAL, COMM, SLACKER FROM EMPNULLABLES WHERE DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000) AS t14 INNER JOIN (SELECT SAL, SAL = 4 AS f9 FROM EMPNULLABLES WHERE DEPTNO = 20 AND SAL > 1000 GROUP BY SAL, SAL = 4) AS t17 ON t14.SAL = t17.SAL OR t17.f9 GROUP BY t14.SAL, t17.SAL, t17.f9 HAVING t17.SAL = t14.SAL) AS t20 ON t12.SAL = t20.SAL0 AND t12.f9 = t20.f9
rewritten_query:
SELECT SAL
FROM EMPNULLABLES
WHERE DEPTNO = 20
  AND SAL > 1000

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Removed the redundant outer WHERE SAL > 1000 (already applied in the innermost subquery t11).
The expression SAL = 4 (aliased f9) is always FALSE for rows satisfying SAL > 1000, so all f9-based join conditions and comparisons are vacuous and were removed.
Collapsed the nested derived tables t11/t12 into a single scan of EMPNULLABLES.

The self-join block t14 ⋈ t17 with OR join condition and GROUP BY/HAVING collapses to a distinct list of SAL from the same filtered set; since it cannot filter or multiply t12 rows, the entire join is eliminated.
Replaced the four-scan, self-joining, grouped query with a single filtered scan; additionally an index on (DEPTNO, SAL) would support the selective filter on the 45M-row table.
